battle.title: Stack Tower Climb
battle.description: Climb the monotonic stack: pop, compare and find the next greater value.

questions.text: In a next-greater-element scan the stack stays in decreasing order. The current number x is greater than the top. What happens?
options: Push x on top without popping anything
Pop the top (x is its answer) and keep comparing with the new top
Clear the whole stack and then push x
Stop the scan, because the answer was found
questions.answer: Pop the top (x is its answer) and keep comparing with the new top
questions.explanation: Every smaller element on the stack has just found its next greater value, so we pop while x is bigger. Clearing the stack would wrongly assign x to larger elements that are still waiting.
Index 2 (value 5) pops both 2 and 1, so both get 5. Nothing is greater than 5 or than the final 3, so those stay -1.

questions.text: For each of 100000 daily temperatures you must find how many days until a warmer day. Which approach is best?
options: A monotonic stack of indices in a single pass
For each day scan forward until a warmer day is found
Sort the temperatures and binary search each day
A HashMap from temperature to its day number
questions.answer: A monotonic stack of indices in a single pass
questions.explanation: The stack gives O(n) total. The forward scan is O(n^2) on a non-increasing input, which is too slow at this size. Sorting loses the day order the answer depends on.

questions.text: Why is the monotonic stack scan O(n) even though a while loop sits inside the for loop?
options: The inner loop runs at most twice per element
The inner loop only runs when the array is sorted
It is really O(n^2) in the worst case, such as a decreasing array
Each element is pushed once and popped at most once, so total pops are at most n
questions.answer: Each element is pushed once and popped at most once, so total pops are at most n
questions.explanation: Work is counted across the whole scan, not per iteration: n pushes plus at most n pops. A decreasing array causes no pops at all, so it is not a worst case.
The value 4 at index 3 resolves index 2 (distance 1) and then index 0 (distance 3); index 1 is resolved by 2 (distance 1). Index 3 has no greater value after it, so 0.

coding.title: Days Until Warmer
coding.description: Given the temperature of each day, print for every day the number of days you must wait until a strictly warmer day. If no warmer day ever comes, print 0 for that day.
coding.inputDescription: Line 1: n. Line 2: n integers, the temperatures.
coding.outputDescription: n integers separated by single spaces.

debug.title: Equal Elements Trap
debug.description: The program reads n and an array and prints, for each element, the next STRICTLY greater element to its right, or -1 if there is none. It is wrong when the array contains equal values. Input: n then n integers. Output: n integers separated by spaces.
hints: Run it on the input '3' then '2 2 3'. Which element is wrong?
Look at the condition that decides when to pop from the stack.
Equal values are being treated as 'greater'. The comparison is not strict.
Change <= to < so an element is popped only by a strictly greater value.
